questions.explanation: find -type d selects only directories and passes them to chmod. chmod -R would also make every regular file executable, and the glob only reaches the top level.

questions.text: Which command changes the owner of script.sh to user alice and its group to devs in one step?
questions.explanation: chown user:group sets both at once; chgrp changes only the group. chmod changes permission bits, not ownership.

questions.text: Which command grants user bob read and write access to report.txt through an ACL, keeping existing ACL entries?
questions.explanation: setfacl -m (modify) adds or updates one entry and leaves others intact. -x removes entries, and getfacl only displays ACLs.

questions.text: Which command removes only the ACL entry for group sales from budget.xls?
questions.explanation: -x deletes the named entry; no permissions are given in the spec. -b would remove every extended entry, and -m g:sales:--- keeps an entry that denies access.

questions.text: Which command removes all extended ACL entries from data/, keeping only the standard owner, group and other permissions?
questions.explanation: -b (--remove-all) strips named user, named group and mask entries but retains the base permissions. chmod a-rwx would remove the base permissions instead.

questions.text: Which command makes every file later created in project/ grant group devs read and write access by default?
questions.explanation: -d sets a default ACL, which new items in the directory inherit. Without -d, the entry applies only to the directory itself, and setgid changes group ownership, not permissions.

questions.text:
getfacl notes.txt shows the lines below. What access does user joe actually have?

user:joe:rwx        #effective:r--
mask::r--
options: rwx, because named user entries ignore the mask
Read only, because the mask limits named users and groups
No access, because the mask overrides all entries
Read and execute, the default for named users
questions.explanation: The mask is the upper bound for named users, named groups and the owning group. Joe's entry says rwx, but only the bits also present in the mask, r--, take effect.

questions.text: A file has extended ACL entries. What does running chmod g=r on it change?
options: Only the owning group's own ACL entry
Nothing, because chmod is ignored on files with ACLs
It deletes all named ACL entries
The ACL mask, which can reduce named users' and groups' effective access
questions.explanation: With an extended ACL, the group bits shown by ls -l represent the mask. Changing them with chmod therefore changes the mask and limits every named entry.

questions.text: In the DN uid=jdoe,ou=users,dc=example,dc=com, what does ou=users represent?
options: The domain the directory belongs to
The organizational unit (container) that holds the entry
questions.explanation: A DN is read from the most specific part to the most general, like a path: uid=jdoe is the entry, ou=users its container, and dc=example,dc=com the domain.

questions.text: What is the conventional base DN for a directory serving the domain example.com?
questions.explanation: Each part of the DNS name becomes a domain component (dc). Searches and new entries are placed under this base, such as ou=users,dc=example,dc=com.

questions.text: Which TCP ports do plain LDAP and LDAP over SSL (LDAPS) use by default?
questions.explanation: LDAP listens on 389, where StartTLS can upgrade the connection, and LDAPS uses TLS from the start on 636. Ports 53/853 are DNS, 88/464 are Kerberos and 443/8443 are HTTPS.

questions.text: Which command searches the subtree dc=example,dc=com for the user jdoe using simple authentication?
questions.explanation: -x selects simple authentication, -b sets the search base, and the filter comes after it. ldapadd creates entries and ldapwhoami only tests a bind.

questions.text: Which LDAP filter matches entries that are of class person and have an email address?
questions.explanation: LDAP filters use prefix notation: & is AND, | is OR and ! is NOT. (mail=*) is a presence test that matches any entry with a mail attribute.

questions.text: Which file format is used to add, modify or export LDAP entries in bulk with tools such as ldapadd and ldapmodify?
questions.explanation: LDIF (LDAP Data Interchange Format) is plain text listing a dn: line followed by attributes. For example, ldapadd -x -D "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com" -W -f user.ldif loads it.

questions.text: A user entry in LDAP has only the inetOrgPerson object class, and getent passwd jdoe returns nothing. What is missing for Linux login?
options: The posixAccount object class with uidNumber, gidNumber, homeDirectory and loginShell
questions.explanation: inetOrgPerson describes a person, but NSS needs POSIX attributes to build a Unix account. Adding posixAccount (and often shadowAccount) with those attributes lets getent passwd jdoe resolve.
